results.title: Where to Rent an H100 PCIe at the Cheapest Price (Oct 2026)
results.author: GPUBank Research
highlights:
The H100 PCIe is the cheapest way to rent 80 GB of Hopper memory on a single card, and that is why it is sold one GPU at a time by so many specialised clouds. It is also the variant that price lists describe most loosely. A row that says only 'H100' can mean this PCIe card, the 94 GB H100 NVL or an SXM module inside an eight-GPU HGX server, three products with different memory, bandwidth and throughput, and a price comparison that mixes them compares nothing. On this page every row says which variant it is, and where the provider does not say, we say that too.

The posted prices for an H100 PCIe hour ran from $0.81 to $3.50 at managed and marketplace providers when we checked on 15 and 16 October 2026, and the spread is mostly about what the hour buys rather than the silicon. Some prices cover the GPU alone, some include a full machine with disk, an IP address and traffic, some can be taken back with a few minutes of notice, and some require a three-year commitment. Stock was thin: Runpod, Lambda, GPU.ai and Oblivus were all shown out of stock, and Vast.ai's own page listed no offers on 16 October 8 7 6.

...

The H100 PCIe is NVIDIA's GH100 Hopper GPU on a full-height, full-length, dual-slot PCI Express Gen5 card with a passive heatsink, built to slot into an ordinary air-cooled server. NVIDIA's product brief gives it 80 GB of HBM2e on a 5,120-bit bus at 2,000 GB/s, a total board power of 350 W, both as default and as maximum, and three NVLink bridge connectors that join two cards at 600 GB/s 9. NVIDIA's datasheet lists 1,513 TFLOPS of BF16 and 3,026 TFLOPS of FP8 on ... tensor cores, but those figures are shown with structured sparsity and the footnote says they are half without it ... are about 756 and 1,513 TFLOPS; the same sheet gives 26 TFLOPS of FP64 and 51 of

...

Reserved capacity is where the terms vary most. GPUBank reserves a single card for a week or a month at $1.08, Hyperstack shows reservations 'starting from' $1.75 without stating the term, and Civo's $1.99 and Oblivus's $2.56 both require 36 months 1 4 3 7. Longer terms buy less than you might expect: ComputePrices listed Impossible Cloud at $2.09 per GPU-hour on 29 September, but for a whole eight-GPU server held for 12 months 8. Serverless is the fifth kind: Beam bills the H100 PCIe at $0.000972 per second of GPU time, about $3.50 an hour, with CPU and memory charged separately, which suits spiky traffic and costs too much for a model that serves all day 2. The comparison table keeps these groups apart, because a marketplace headline at $2.00 and a managed all-in price at $2.00 buy different things.

### The rest of the market

Beyond the six providers above, the rest of the market is a long tail of smaller clouds whose prices we could read only through trackers. ComputePrices showed QuantaCloud at $2.59 in the US Midwest, Omega Gradient at $2.63 in Canada, OVHcloud at $2.99 for its h100-380 flavour, which pairs the card with 30 vCPU, 380 GB of RAM and 3.84 TB of passthrough NVMe and reports itself to nvidia-smi as 'NVIDIA H100 PCIe' in Spare Cores' test 12, and AtmosCompute at $3.01, with Thunder Compute at $3.20 in an older reading dated 5 September, and GetDeploying showed Scaleway's single-card H100-1-80G at $3.21 in stock in Paris and Warsaw, Oblivus at $3.50 out of stock and Enverge at $4.00 8 13 7. Scaleway's own page confirms that both its flavours carry the PCIe card, with 24 vCPU and 240 GB of RAM on the single-GPU one, but did not show a price when we read it 14. io.net's own price guide, dated April 2026, gives $1.49 for an H100 PCIe on its decentralised network, a snapshot we could not refresh 15.

The marketplace readings move by the hour, so their history says more than any single number. GridCompute, which tracks Vast.ai hourly, counted four on-demand H100 PCIe listings with eight GPUs between them on 8 October, with a lowest ask of $1.25 and a median of $2.78, and the median had ranged from $1.63 to $3.52 since tracking began on 2 October 16. On the interruptible side GetDeploying showed a two-card Vast.ai listing in South Africa at $0.67 per GPU on 15 October, and Beam's own H100 article puts Vast.ai's interruptible offers 'around $0.35 per GPU-hour' 5 17. Lium, whose price includes the node's local disk, was tracked at $1.40 in Almaty on 29 September and at $2.15 in Boardman in the United States, with 26 vCPU and 221 GB of RAM, on 7 October 18. None of these hours comes with a fixed machine or a credit when the host goes away, and on Vast.ai the disk and bandwidth are billed on top of the ask 11.

Massed Compute sells an 'H100 (80GB)' at $2.73 an hour with 20 vCPU, 128 GB of RAM and 1,250 GB of storage, next to separate rows for the H100 NVL and the H100 SXM5, so by elimination it is the PCIe card even though the page never says so 19. On the marketplace side, Lium had no H100 PCIe free when we looked, only SXM listings, and OpenRelay was tracked at $2.20 20 8. None of these is a reason to skip the providers above, but QuantaCloud and Massed Compute are worth a look if you need a US machine with a large local disk and the cheaper clouds are sold out.

### 02 How much does an H100 PCIe cost per hour?

On 15 and 16 October 2026 an H100 PCIe cost between $1.35 and $3.50 an hour on demand at managed clouds, about $2.00 on marketplaces with stock and from $0.81 on interruptible capacity. The managed prices we read at source were GPUBank $1.35, Beam from $1.83, Civo $2.49, Hyperstack $2.50, Massed Compute $2.73, Runpod Secure Cloud $2.89 and Lambda $3.29 1 2 3 4 19 29 26. GPUBank's own survey of public on-demand prices put the market average at $2.71 on 29 September 41. A full 730-hour month therefore runs from $985.50 to about $2,400 before storage, and the large clouds do not sell this card at all.

results.title: QuantaCloud GPU 怎么选？A100、H100、L40S 和按秒退款规则讲清楚 | 智机玄同
results.author: 智机玄同 发布于 2026年10月9日 3 分钟阅读
highlights:
QuantaCloud 提供按需 GPU VM，启动先预扣一小时，停止后退回未用秒数。本文解释 A100 SXM/PCIe、H100、L40S 的当前配置和数据删除规则。

智机玄同发布于 2026年10月9日 3 分钟阅读

资料核查日期： 2026年10月9日。价格、库存和服务商规则可能变化，请以官方页面为准。

文章目录

QuantaCloud 的计费方式有点特别。

它不是“每秒从余额里一点点扣”，而是：

启动时先扣一小时，停止时再把这一小时里没用掉的秒数退回来。

所以最终效果仍然是按实际运行秒数结算。

官方 FAQ 说得很清楚：跑 3 小时 17 分钟，最后就是付 3 小时 17 分钟。

## 当前公开单卡价格

截至 2026-10-09，QuantaCloud 当前 pricing catalog 里比较重要的单 GPU 配置包括：

- A100 PCIe 80GB：$1.48 / 小时
- A100 SXM4 80GB：$1.50 / 小时
- L40S 48GB：$1.09 / 小时
- H100 PCIe 80GB：$2.69 / 小时

这些不是单独一张 GPU 的裸价。

官方页面明确说明，小时价包含整台 VM 的 GPU、vCPU、RAM 和本地磁盘。

...

## H100 PCIe 单卡

当前 pricing catalog 的 1× H100 PCIe：

- 20 vCPU
- 128GB RAM
- 1,250GB 本地磁盘
- $2.69 / 小时

这条会进入现有 H100 PCIe Compare。

## 最大的坑不是价格，而是磁盘

QuantaCloud 当前 On-Demand VM 有一条必须提前知道：

Stop 会终止 VM，并删除它的本地磁盘。

官方当前也说明没有持久卷和 Snapshot。

所以你不能像普通 VPS 那样随便关机，然后几天后回来继续。

模型、checkpoint、输出文件如果还要保留，停止以前要先复制出去。

这对训练任务尤其重要。

results.title: Crusoe H100 went $3.90 to $4.50 an hour, H200 $5.40, October 15, 2026
highlights:
Crusoe’s pricing page raised two on-demand GPU rates between our reads of October 15, 2026 at 14:40 and 15:40 UTC. The H100 80GB HGX went from $3.90 to $4.50 a GPU-hour (+15.4%) and the H200 141GB HGX from $4.29 to $5.40 (+25.9%). In the same read the page gave an on-demand rate for the B200 180GB HGX for the first time since we started reading it on September 13: $8.50 a GPU-hour.

...

Both old figures had been the same in every hourly read since September 13. The H100 rose by $4.50 - $3.90 = $0.60 a GPU-hour and the H200 by $5.40 - $4.29 = $1.11. Over a 730-hour month on one GPU, the H100 rate went from $2,847 ($3.90 × 730) to $3,285 ($4.50 × 730). An 8-GPU HGX node at the new H100 rate lists at $36.00 an hour ($4.50 × 8).

Three other rates in the same table kept their figures in the same reads: the A100 80GB PCIe at $2.00, the L40S at $1.50 and the AMD MI300X at $3.45.

results.title: What It Actually Costs to Rent an H100, H200, or B200 in October 2026
results.author: Dex Mareno
highlights:
- As of late October 2026, the cheapest reliable on-demand H100 (80GB) is back around $1.99/GPU-hr (Voltage Park), with brand-name specialty clouds at ~$2.50 (Hyperstack PCIe), ~$2.89 (RunPod), and ~$2.90 SXM (Ori); the median 'cheapest' across two dozen providers is ~$3.33, and spot dips to ~$0.94 (Prime Intellect). Hyperscaler H100 is still ~$10–13/hr.
- H200 (141GB) firmed since September: neocloud floors run ~$3.14–3.99 (Prime Intellect ~$3.14, Spheron ~$3.35, Theta ~$3.69, Hyperbolic ~$3.99), the Ornn transacted index settled at $5.24 on Oct 12, and getdeploying's on-demand median is ~$5.00 across 33 providers. Spot ~$2.29. Hyperscaler H200 is ~$7.91–13.78.
- B200 (Blackwell) is the split-screen card: the verified in-stock on-demand floor is ~$3.75 (Packet.ai, per getdeploying on Oct 22) — essentially flat versus September's ~$3.70 — but the on-demand MEDIAN is now ~$7.99–8.19 (RunPod $7.99, Together $8.19). Spot from ~$3.20 (Vultr).
- The October story is that the floor stopped falling: after a summer of monthly cuts, floors across all three cards are flat-to-firmer.
- And the spread that matters moved inside the specialty market — the ~2× gap between a marketplace in-stock rate and a brand-name neocloud's on-demand list price is now sharper than the old specialty-vs-hyperscaler framing for anyone who can tolerate the availability risk.
- The decision is still utilization, not sticker: below ~40–50% duty cycle a per-token API almost always beats renting metal.
